focus.label: Benign nevoid/segmental skin lesion
focus.why: Young age and segmental pattern support nevoid lesion; no systemic symptoms favors benign local process. Pruritus/excoriation is atypical but possible.

payload.query: Need the histopathological report of a skin biopsy from the lesional plaque, as it is the core evidence to distinguish a benign nevoid/segmental lesion from chronic inflammatory dermatosis by revealing architectural pattern, epidermal changes, and inflammatory infiltrate.

payload.analysis: Combined with the suspected benign nevoid/segmental lesion, histopathology reveals follicular and sebaceous epithelial mucin deposition with Alcian blue positivity, accompanied only by a mild lymphocytic infiltrate and no cytological atypia or epidermotropism. This supports follicular mucinosis, a benign chronic inflammatory/nevoid process, and refutes infection or systemic disease. Pruritus and excoriation are consistent with secondary inflammation. All key clinical and histopathological information is covered.

payload.analysis: Pathology reveals follicular mucinosis with perivascular lymphocytes, no atypia or epidermotropism, supporting benign follicular mucinosis over a nevoid lesion. Clinical segmental pattern and chronic pruritic course fit this inflammatory dermatosis. Absence of systemic symptoms and normal development confirm benignity. T-cell receptor rearrangement remains pending, but histology effectively excludes mycosis fungoides. All key histopathologic information is covered.

why.why: Histopathology demonstrates follicular and sebaceous epithelial mucin deposition with Alcian blue positivity, mild lymphocytic infiltrate, and no atypia or epidermotropism, which is characteristic of follicular mucinosis, a chronic inflammatory dermatosis. The clinical segmental pruritic pattern and absence of systemic symptoms fit this entity, and both the Pathologist and Radiologist analyses support it. Confidence is increased from 0.4 to 0.9.

payload.query: Need the T-cell receptor gene rearrangement study results from the skin biopsy specimen, as this molecular test is the critical next step to confirm polyclonal (reactive) versus clonal T-cell population, thereby distinguishing benign follicular mucinosis from early mycosis fungoides and firmly validating the chronic inflammatory dermatosis diagnosis.
